question: A paediatric intern is counselling parents about vaccines given at 9 months. She explains that one of the vaccines given at this visit is a live-attenuated virus vaccine and must be given at least 4 weeks apart from other live vaccines. Which vaccine is she referring to?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: PCV is a conjugate (non-live) vaccine. It does not carry live-vaccine interval restrictions.
The inactivated Hepatitis A vaccine is non-live and does not require a minimum interval from other live vaccines.

Correct. MR vaccine is a live-attenuated viral vaccine given at 9–12 months (first dose) under NIS. Live vaccines require a minimum 4-week interval from other live vaccines to avoid immune interference.
fIPV is an inactivated (killed) poliovirus vaccine. As a non-live vaccine, it has no minimum interval restriction from other live vaccines.

overallFeedback.feedback: Classify vaccines by antigen type: live-attenuated (BCG, OPV, MR, Rotavirus, JE-live) carry unique handling and interval requirements that non-live vaccines do not.
MR is live-attenuated; PCV and fIPV are non-live. Live vaccines must be separated by ≥4 weeks if not given simultaneously.
